note: Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-11-03T03:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is field line opening seen along the NE limb in GOES SUVI 195 and 284 beginning at approx. 2025-11-03T02:40Z. This CME is overtaken by CME: 2025-11-03T04:36Z as it progresses further into the field-of-view.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. This event is not measurable in GOES CCOR-1 due to an eclipse.

note: CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-11-03T04:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is wide opening field lines seen in GOES SUVI 193 and 284 beginning at approx. 2025-11-03T04:00Z, associated with a C7.1 flare from AR 14274 (N25E85) which peaked at 2025-11-03T04:30Z. This CME overtakes previous CME: 2025-11-03T03:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Large partial halo CME visible to the E/NE in SOHO LASCO C2 (for a few frames before a data gap), GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is an M1.6 class flare from AR 14274 (N25E90) with associated filament ejecta, moving/opening field lines, a rising loop, post-eruptive arcades and possible EUV wave as seen in GOES SUVI wavelengths 195, 284, 131, 304, 171. A separate M5.0 class flare follows the first flare closely which appears to have been the source of the EUV wave and may contribute to the shock structure associated with this CME, especially the SE portion of it. The EUV wave is best seen in GOES SUVI 195 spreading towards the coronal hole visible nearing the central Earth-facing disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: These parameters are based on the best fit of the BULK of the CME using GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Some deflection may have occurred with the nearby negative polarity coronal hole feature visible on the Earth-facing solar disk.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: This CME is visible to the south in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is seen as moving/opening field lines along the southern limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2025-11-03T11:28Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is back-to-back M-class flares from AR 14274 (N22E74) as seen in GOES SUVI 131 and 284 starting at 2025-11-03T12:19Z. This CME follows in the path of the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2025-11-03T09:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: These parameters are based on the best fit using SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: A narrow jet-like CME seen to the NE in SOHO, STEREO A and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. No source has been found for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). The source for this event has not been found.

note: CME seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. Source is the C8.7 flare from AR 14274 (N24E59) peaking at 2025-11-04T00:08Z and an associated minor eruption with small ejecta seen in STEREO A EUV 304 on/behind the NE limb at 2025-11-04T00:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very preliminary analysis with early imagery. This analysis is based on the location of the source (C8.7 flare) and on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1).

Final analysis with more imagery. It is based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1) and on the source location of the M3.5 flare. This complex event associated with two flares is treated as a single CME.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-11-04T03:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is continued field line movement and dimming seen located at approx. N20E50 in GOES SUVI 195 following earlier CME: 2025-11-04T00:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. This event is not measurable in GOES CCOR-1 due to an eclipse period.

note: CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-11-04T11:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. Not clearly seen in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a minor eruption and field line opened seen along the Western limb in GOES SUVI/STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 beginning at approx. 2025-11-04T10:06Z. A C4.6 flare from AR 14267 (N01W85) is also visible in association with this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement due to source near the limb and lack of STEREO A COR2 imagery to triangulate.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

note: Halo CME first seen to the NE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-11-04T17:53Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event was an X1.8 flare from Active Region 14274 (N24E63) peaking at 2025-11-04T17:34Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131. Filament material is also visible in association with this flare in GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304, along with field line opening and an EUV wave visible in GOES SUVI 195/284.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK analysis, triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 of the bright bulk feature observed primarily to the NE in all coronagraphs. Measurable SOHO LASCO C2 imagery not yet available due to a downlink gap.

SHOCK analysis, best fit triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 of the faint, wider halo shock in all 3 coronagraphs. Due to the large width of the observed shock front and viewing angle differences between the coronagraphs, this best fit is made using the width in GOES CCOR-1/SOHO LASCO C3 and tracking the edge of the front with less emphasis on the width in COR2A. Measurable SOHO LASCO C2 imagery not yet available due to a downlink gap.

note: CME observed to the SE in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2, not yet in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a downlink gap beginning around 2025-11-04T20:36Z. The source is an X1.1 flare from on or just beyond the SE limb (S15E90) peaking at 2025-11-04T22:01Z observed in GOES SUVI 131. Also observed as a large rising field line loop, EUV wave, and post-eruptive arcade following the flare in GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2; SOHO LASCO C2/C3 not yet available due to ongoing downlink gap. The CME front is somewhat irregularly shaped, as such this triangulation captures the majority of the bulk material as best as possible.

note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2, with a notably irregular diffuse leading edge. The source is an M1.7 flare from AR 14272 (N25E36) peaking at 2025-11-04T22:44Z observed in GOES SUVI 131. Also observed as field line breaking, dimming, and small post eruptive arcades in GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 with some loose filament ejecta in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2, tracking the irregular diffuse bulk material with a best fit as possible, finding a good fit near the flare source region (N25E36).

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2 imagery for a few frames before becoming too diffuse to observe. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. The source may be associated with a small eruption from Active Region 14274 (N30E52) starting around 2025-11-05T05:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME first seen in real time to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2025-11-05T10:53Z. CME is also seen in GOES CCOR-1 as a halo with the bulk to the E. CME was missed by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real time due to a scheduled gap between downlink periods. The CME is most likely associated with a long-duration M7.4 class flare from AR 14274 (N24E47) that peaked at 2025-11-05T11:19Z. The flare and associated eruption can be seen across GOES SUVI wavelengths but is best visible in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best-fit measurement based on limited imagery from STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
Best-fit measurement of the SHOCK feature based on running difference imagery from STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is difficult to observe in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to surrounding outflow. The source for this event is unknown. It is possible this event is associated with an M1.3 flare from a currently unnumbered region near the southeast limb starting around 2025-11-05T12:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131 imagery. However, the timing and southern latitude of the flare make it an unlikely source candidate.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the unknown source location.

note: This CME is visible to the west in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to an eruption visible near the southwestern limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2025-11-05T14:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption north of Active Region 14274 (N40E42) starting around 2025-11-05T15:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 195 and 284 imagery. Dimming is observed north of the eruption site in GOES SUVI 195 imagery around this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not observed in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap. The source of this event is likely far-sided and may be related to a small eruption observed beyond the southeastern limb in GOES SUVI 195/284 imagery starting around 2025-11-05T18:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and unknown source location.

note: This CME is visible to the north/northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery and partially overlaps with the halo CME: 2025-11-05T22:23Z. The source of this event may be related to the impulsive M8.6 flare from Active Region 14274 starting around 2025-11-05T22:00Z, the same source as 2025-11-05T22:23Z, as there appear to be multiple ejections of material associated with this flare which are deflected northward.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible as a full halo directed towards the north/northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is observed as a partial halo directed towards the northeast as seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an M8.6 flare and subsequent eruption from Active Region 14274 (N30E41) starting around 2025-11-05T22:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. Dimming is observed northwest of the eruption site as seen in GOES SUVI 195 imagery, indicating likely northwest deflection of this event. Field line movement is also observed to the northeast as seen in GOES SUVI 195 and 284 imagery. Additionally, post eruptive arcades are visible starting around 2025-11-05T23:00Z in GOES SUVI 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the inner, brighter bulk portion based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
SHOCK measurement of the faint, wider feature surrounding the bulk of this event. Measured parameters based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the NE in STEREO A COR2. Source is ejecta seen starting around 2025-11-05T22:36Z in GOES SUVI 304 from AR 14274 (N24E40) with heavy northern deflection. This ejection of material immediately follows the ejecta seen around 2025-11-05T22:00Z which was the source of the preceding CME:2025-11-05T22:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Analysis of this CME was affected by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 lasting from 2025-11-06T01:54Z to 2025-11-06T06:30Z.

note: Faint CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 for a few frames beginning at 2025-11-06T12:48Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 more clearly in later frames. This event is not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C3 or GOES CCOR-1 due to faintness. There is no clear source seen for this CME, as it is likely far sided with respects to both SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the North by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-11-06T14:31Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 due to a data gap which began at 2025-11-06T15:42Z. The source of this event is a region of dimming seen beginning at approx. 2025-11-06T13:52Z located at approx. N45E40, likely exhibiting some NW deflection based on GOES SUVI 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Minor CME seen N in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 and NNE in STEREO A COR2. Its source is  possibly a minor eruption N of AR 14274 with dimming centered around N30E30, best seen in GOES SUVI 195. Another candidate is an even fainter dimming further west, centered around ~N25E20 and starting around 2025-11-06T12:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs. Two possible sources are further to east from the longitude of the fit and much further south, so there is likely a significant deflection to the NW.

note: Minor CME seen to the N in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNE in STEREO A COR. Its source is likely the continuing minor eruption/dimming N of AR 14274 (N24E31), with dimming and minor post-eruptive arcades centered around (~N40E30), best seen in GOES SUVI 195 starting around 2025-11-06T12:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1).

note: Very faint, minor CME seen to the N in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNE in STEREO A COR2. Its source is best seen in GOES SUVI 195 and might be the continuing minor eruption/dimming N of AR 14274 (N24E31) with dimming and minor post-eruptive arcades centered around (~N40E35) starting as early as 2025-11-06T12:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs.

note: This CME is visible to the east/northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery only. The source may be related to a minor eruption near Active Region 14274 (N27E31) which deflects northward starting around 2025-11-07T02:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. However, this source is speculative. As this CME is not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery it is difficult to confirm the source.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 41 degrees with STEREO A COR2 imagery as the source location is speculative and this event is not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. While the bulk of this event is directed towards the northeast, a faint halo feature is produced from the shock of this CME. The source is an M1.7 flare from Active Region 14274 (N27E27) starting around 2025-11-07T07:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 imagery. Dimming is observed north of the eruption site in GOES SUVI 195 imagery, with minor field line movement visible over the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 195/284 imagery. This eruption can be observed near the northeast limb in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the bright northeast bulk feature based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
SHOCK measurement of the fainter halo feature, which surrounds the brighter northeast bulk feature, based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the north in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to an eruption centered near N40E30, which appears to deflect to the northwest, starting around 2025-11-07T10:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304 and STEREO A EUVI imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption northeast of Active Region 14274 (N35E30) starting around 2025-11-07T12:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. An EUV wave is observed northeast of the eruption site as seen in GOES SUVI 195 imagery, with a wide opening of field lines observed over the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 195/284 imagery. Post eruptive arcades begin to form around 2025-11-07T14:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 171/195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Narrow, jet-like CME first seen to the SW in COR2A only starting at 2025-11-07T23:08Z. This CME is much easier to distinguish in running difference imagery. There is no visible source of this CME on the Earth-facing disk or in STA EUVI imagery, so this source is very likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement from the perspective of STEREO A which is ~49 degrees west of Earth.

note: Halo CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-11-09T07:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and in the NE by STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is an X1.7 flare from Active Region 14274 (N27E03) which peaked at 2025-11-09T07:35Z seen in GOES SUVI 131. Dimming and field line movement associated with this flare seen in GOES SUVI 171, 193 and 284 appears to have a Northwestern trajectory, suggesting the possibility of deflection. This CME has appears to have a very asymmetric morphology from the perspective of SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There does not appear to be a shock feature associated with this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Faint CME first seen to the South by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-11-09T12:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, and to the SE by STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This event is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen located at approx. S25E25 in GOES SUVI 304, with lift off beginning around 2025-11-09T12:20Z. Dimming seen in GOES SUVI 195 suggests a possible Southern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Slow, wide, likely streamer blowout CME lacking defined front seen to the North by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-11-09T13:25Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event appears to be some continued field line movement and opening following X1.7 flare and eruption which peaked at 2025-11-09T07:35Z as seen in GOES SUVI 195 and 285.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: CME first seen to the West in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-11-09T13:48Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a slow rising prominence seen along the West limb in GOES SUVI 304 and on the Western disk in STEREO A EUVI 304 (approx. N00W100) starting as early as 2025-11-09T06:45Z. This CME is likely deflected due to proximity to a coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: This CME is faint but visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery for a few frames before becoming too diffuse to observe. The CME is not visible in GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely far-sided as there are no signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the south in STEREO A COR2, and to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is a filament eruption observed near the southwest limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery which begins to lift off around 2025-11-09T22:00Z. A subsequent opening of field lines can be observed over the southwest limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is seen starting slowly to the W/NW in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1. The source is a filament eruption observed near or beyond the northwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2025-11-09T22:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. The CME initially measured less than 200 km/s but was reanalyzed with later frames and sped up significantly.

note: Narrow, relatively slow CME embedded within the core of slow CME first seen at 2025-11-10T00:48Z seen in the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2; the source is far-sided as evidenced by moving field lines seen around 2025-11-10T03:00Z in GOES SUVI 284 off the west limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2A.

note: Halo CME seen in SOHO LASCO C2, SOHO LASCO C3, and GOES CCOR-1 and wide CME seen predominantly to the northeast in STEREO A COR2A in association with an eruptive X1.2-class solar flare from Active Region 14274 (N25W16). The solar flare is best seen in GOES SUVI 131 and a faint circular EUV wave is seen propagating shortly following the flare in GOES SUVI 195 and 284 angstrom imagers.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement of the bulk with very few frames.
Measurement of the shock front out to 13 solar radii.
Updated bulk measurement out to 25 solar radii.

note: Seemingly narrow eruption to the N from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1's perspective, but appears wider and more to the N/NE in STEREO A COR2's field of view. From STEREO A's perspective, it drifts N as it moves out in the field of view. The source appears to be an eruption associated with filament ejecta visible to the N/NW from AR 14274 around 2025-11-10T12:00Z as seen in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit, however the feature continues to drift north in the STEREO A COR2 field of view and may have a more northern deflection in later frames not properly captured in this measurement.

note: Large halo CME first seen to the NE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-11-11T10:23Z, as well as to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is an X5.1 flare from Active Region 14274 (N27W27) which peaked at 2025-11-11T10:04Z as seen in GOES SUVI 131. Wide opening field lines and a large EUV wave and instance of dimming is visible in GOES SUVI 195 and 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195, along with post eruptive arcades visible in GOES SUVI 131 and 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: This CME/outflow is visible to the northwest in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is difficult to observe in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery due to particle contamination from high proton fluxes following the 2025-11-11T09:45Z solar energetic particle event. The source is unknown as this event is likely outflow following CME: 2025-11-11T10:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the unknown source location and difficulty in observing this event in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME/outflow is visible to the northwest in GOES CCOR-1 and to the northeast STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event is difficult to observe in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery due to particle contamination from high proton fluxes following the 2025-11-11T09:45Z solar energetic particle event. The source is unknown as this event is likely outflow following CME: 2025-11-11T10:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME/outflow is visible to the north in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is difficult to observe in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery due to particle contamination from high proton fluxes following the 2025-11-11T09:45Z solar energetic particle event. The source is unknown as this event is likely outflow following CME: 2025-11-11T10:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the uncertain source location and difficulty in observing this event in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery for a few frames before becoming too diffuse to observe. The source may be related to a minor eruption centered near N10W70 as seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting around 2025-11-11T15:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME first seen to the NNW in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2025-11-12T17:45Z. This CME is also faintly seen to the N in STEREO A COR2 for a couple frames. This event is difficult to observe in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery due to particle contamination from high proton fluxes following the 2025-11-11T11:09Z solar energetic particle event detected at SOHO. The source is most likely a filament eruption beginning around 2025-11-12T16:00Z from near AR 14274 that appears to be deflected northward. The CME is also likely associated with a C4.5 flare from AR 14274 peaking at 2025-11-12T16:39Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best-fit measurement based on GOES CCOR-1 and limited imagery from STEREO A COR2.

note: Extremely faint CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 but too faint to be seen in C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Its source may potentially be the minor eruption in AR 4274 (N24W51), directed northward and seen in GOES SUVI 304 at 2025-11-13T01:15Z, however the fit with two coronagraphs indicates that the CME is far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs indicates the source should be behind the NW limb, however no source has been found in STEREO A EUV imagery to confirm this fit. Because of the extreme faintness of the CME and the lack of coronal signatures these parameters are rather speculative.

note: CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen at all in STEREO A coronagraph. The source of it could be a C6.1 flare from AR 14274 (N24W51) peaking at 2025-11-13T03:34Z, however no clear eruption/coronal signatures of the CME have been seen in EUV imagery associated with this flare.

cmeAnalyses.note: This analysis was made with one coronagraph based on the location of C6.1 flare from Active Region 14274 as one potential source. However, there is no eruption seen in association with the flare. The CME is not seen in STEREO A coronagraph, so this analysis is rather speculative.

note: This CME is visible to the east/southeast in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery for a few frames before becoming too diffuse to observe. It is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely far-sided and may be related to a faint opening of field lines observed over the east/southeast limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting around 2025-11-13T08:50Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is related to an eruption from Active Region 14247 (N30W58) which exhibits clear northern deflection as seen in GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2025-11-13T14:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption spanning S30E50 to S25E05 which begins to lift off around 2025-11-13T17:30Z as seen in GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. Dimming is observed south of the eruption starting around 2025-11-13T18:30Z in GOES SUVI 195 imagery, and post eruptive arcades can be seen starting around 2025-11-13T19:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Noting that this event is partially obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event overlaps with preceding CME: 2025-11-13T18:38Z. The source may be related to an eruption centered near S20E55 starting around 2025-11-13T19:40Z seen best in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. However, it is also possible this event is associated with the southeast filament eruption which was associated with CME: 2025-11-13T18:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the SSE in STEREO A COR2. Source is likely beyond the southeast limb of the Earth-facing disk. A rising loop of material may possibly be seen at 2025-11-13T23:35Z in STEREO A EUVI 195 from beyond the southeast limb. There are no source signatures discernable in GOES SUVI imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 and the candidate source location seen in available UV imagery.

note: Asymmetric halo seen with bulk to the northwest with a faint halo-shaped shock in SOHO LASCO C2/LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 with wider bulk seen to the north and northwest in STEREO A COR2A associated with an X4.0-class solar flare from AR14274 (N24W71). The eruption is characterized by brightening seen best in GOES SUVI 131 and as well in GOES SUVI 195 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery with a significant, rapid field line movement and darkening seen off the northwest limb around 2025-11-14T07:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement of the bulk of the CME using limited SOHO LASCO C2/C3 frames and STEREO A COR2 out to 17 solar radii.
Measurement of the SHOCK feature using the best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
Measurement of the BULK using source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Faint loop CME seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the N in STEREO A COR2. Source is uncertain, but may possibly be a narrow piece of ejecta originating from AR 14274 (N22W69), but with heavy northern deflection, seen at about 2025-11-14T09:00Z in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using candidate source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Jet-like CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the N in STEREO A COR2. Source is a small instance of brightening seen at about N22W80 from AR 14274 (N24W72) seen in GOES SUVI 304 at 2025-11-14T14:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

note: CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the W in STEREO A COR2. Source is gradually opening field lines and a wide rising loop seen faintly on or just beyond the West limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2025-11-14T13:02Z and continuing through about 2025-11-14T15:06Z. A small area of gradual dimming can be seen at about N00W94 in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery starting as early as 2025-11-14T11:35Z and gradually evolving through about 2025-11-14T15:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Narrow CME seen to the northwest in GOES CCOR-1 and due north in STEREO A COR2A in association with a filament eruption occurring near N35W65 around 2025-11-14T19:20Z, best seen as a lifting plasma channel in GOES SUVI 304. Not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a data gap.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2A.

note: Faint CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2025-11-15T01:36Z. CME is also seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. There is not a clear source for this CME; however, it is possibly related to a small eruption from AR 14274 best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2025-11-15T01:20Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best-fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

note: CME first seen to the SSE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2025-11-15T04:36Z. CME can also be seen to the SSE in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. The imagery in GOES CCOR-1 is partially obscured by the pylon. There are two source candidates for this CME. The first is associated with field line movement over the SE limb that can be seen across GOES SUVI wavelengths for a few hours prior to the emergence into SOHO LASCO C2.  The second is a small filament eruption beginning around 2025-11-15T02:04Z best seen in GOES SUVI 304 centered around AR 14279 (~S13W11).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best-fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. There is some uncertainty in this measurement due to deflection within the FOV. The CME also appears to accelerate about half-way through the FOV of SOHO LASCO C3.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2025-11-15T05:00Z. CME is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is most likely a small filament eruption centered around N30E50 best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2025-11-15T04:00Z. This CME is somewhat faint in white light imagery as it is along a NE streamer.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best-fit measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Faint CME with a fuzzy front to the NW, seen mostly in SOHO LASCO C2 (disappearing after a few timestamps) and in GOES CCOR-1. The CME is fully covered by the large daily data gap in STEREO A coronagraph. Its source is likely a minor prominence eruption off the NW limb seen in GOES SUVI 304 at 2025-11-15T19:08Z. The source of this eruption is most likely AR 4274 (N24W88). This event may also be associated with the C1.7 flare from this active region, peaking at 2025-11-15T22:51Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate, one-coronagraph (SOHO LASCO C2) analysis based on the location of AR 4274. Not confirmed by STEREO A coronagraph as the CME is fully covered by the data gap starting at 2025-11-15T11:40Z.

note: CME directed NNW in SOHO and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs, with two consecutive fronts (either a shock and a bulk or two consecutive CMEs). Not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2. Source is likely a filament eruption centered at (N45W20) seen as dimming and significant area of post-eruptive arcades centered around this area in GOES SUVI 195, and as slowly rising northern ejecta in SUVI 304 seen after 2025-11-15T21:20Z. The erupting filament seems to be ~30-40 degrees in length.

cmeAnalyses.note: A tentative analysis with one coronagraph (SOHO LASCO), based on a very approximate source location (N45W20). In the absence of STEREO A imagery due to long data gap this is the best that can be done.

Approximate analysis of the second front of this CME (likely its bulk) with one coronagraph analysis method (using SOHO) and based on the approximate location of the source - an erupting 30-40 long northern filament. STEREO A imagery is not available for this event.
